title: Kahana vs Telegram: Living Room vs Library
excerpt: Telegram is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. Kahana is the shelf and reading list beside the chat, not another inbox.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: One of the top three messaging apps globally, with 700M+ MAUs reported in recent years.
Widely used for large public channels, groups (up to 200k members), and private chats.
Monetization evolving via Telegram Ads revenue share and Stars (in-app currency) for mini-apps and memberships.

strengths.title: Large-group friendly: groups and channels
strengths.detail: Huge groups (up to 200k) and broadcast channels with unlimited subscribers, suited to large semi-public communities.

strengths.title: Strong mobile experience
strengths.detail: Fast, responsive app praised for balancing features and simplicity on mobile.

strengths.title: Privacy and security focus
strengths.detail: Secret Chats (E2E), self-destruct timers, and a strong reputation among privacy-minded users.

strengths.title: Bots and automation
strengths.detail: Rich bot ecosystem for moderation, notifications, and workflows, common in crypto, trading, and tech communities.

weaknesses.title: Limited structure beyond chat
weaknesses.detail: Mostly group chats or broadcast channels, no native spaces, rich threads, or course/community structures like Circle or Mighty.

weaknesses.title: Branding and customization constraints
weaknesses.detail: Little branding beyond channel name/photo; no white-label apps or custom domains.

weaknesses.title: Monetization still emerging
weaknesses.detail: Stars and ad revenue share are relatively new; no mature native membership-tier system like Patreon.

weaknesses.title: Limited moderation and anti-abuse tools
weaknesses.detail: Lighter safety controls than Slack or dedicated community platforms; large groups can be hard to manage.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Telegram is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Cloud-based mobile and desktop messaging focused on security and speed, often described as hitting a sweet spot between Discord and Slack with a strong mobile experience.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Telegram side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Telegram you can use Memberships and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Telegram

You can use both. Telegram keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Telegram. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
